sources.entry: Azimutt - Visual database exploration made for real world databases (big and messy). Explore your database schema as well as data, document them, extend them and even get analysis and guidelines. (Demo, Source Code) MIT Elixir/Nodejs/Docker

summary.one_liner: Azimutt is an open-source, full-stack database exploration tool that provides visual ERD diagrams, data navigation, documentation, and schema analysis for large, messy real-world databases.
summary.what_it_does: Azimutt lets you design a schema using AML for fast diagramming, and explore it with search-everywhere, showing only useful tables and columns while following relations. It can query data by following foreign keys and displaying entities in the diagram. Documentation features include table and column notes and tags, layouts, and memos for use cases, features, or team scopes. It also analyzes a database to surface inconsistencies and suggest best practices. The README also describes loading any public SQL file in Azimutt via a URL parameter, which can be linked from a repository as a badge.
use_cases: explore a large database schema visually
generate an interactive ERD for a SQL file in a repo
document tables and columns with notes and tags
follow foreign keys while browsing data
analyze a database for inconsistencies and best practices
how_to_run: Self-hosted: use the Docker image (full guide linked in README)
Local development: install pnpm, Elm, elm-spa, Elixir/Phoenix, and PostgreSQL
notable: Visual ERD designed for large, messy real-world schemas with hundreds of tables
Schema design with AML text-based diagramming
Load any public SQL file into the explorer via a URL parameter for embeddable badges
Built-in whole-database analysis for inconsistencies and best practices
Documentation layer with table/column notes, tags, layouts, and memos
caveats: Local development requires a multi-language toolchain (Elixir, Elm, Node/pnpm, PostgreSQL) and a configured .env file
Stripe payment setup is needed for paid-feature testing locally, per the README's Stripe section
Heroku and Kubernetes deployment require extra manual steps (Stackhero S3 bucket, config vars, or a separate guide)
